generations.name: C1 (2019-2023, vor Facelift)
generations.notes: The rear bench slides 140 mm. The trunk holds 455 l with the bench all the way forward (the ADAC 'normal' value) and 385 l with it all the way back, per VW figures quoted by Motor1. With the rear seats folded it holds 1281 l, measured to the roof. Width: ADAC gives 1782 mm, AMS gives 1760 mm; VW.de gives 1760-1784 mm depending on trim. Height: ADAC, AMS and the VW press release from March 2019 give 1584 mm (likely with roof rails). The VW world-premiere release from 2018 gave 1558 mm and a 2563 mm wheelbase, but later VW and ADAC data say 2551 mm. Only front-wheel drive was offered. Germany: orders from 12/2018, deliveries from 04/2019; ADAC lists this series until 10/2023.

data.notes: The research stopped early: the shared web-search budget for this run (200 calls) ran out partway through. All values come from searches made before that; null values and the notFound list mark the gaps. A follow-up run could fill them, starting with the new T-Roc (2025) fact sheet on volkswagen-newsroom.com, which was found but not read in detail. Trunk volumes are VDA manufacturer values (ADAC 'normal'). The T-Cross and Golf Sportsvan have sliding rear benches: trunkL is the bench-forward value, and the bench-back value is in the notes. ADAC's own measured trunk values are lower and were not used. No other Volkswagen models were added. The Tera is not sold in Germany, and the ID. Cross (BEV small SUV) was not researched because its German market launch could not be confirmed and it likely belongs to the ID. model list. One source URL for the T-Roc Cabriolet 1.5 TSI test page was inferred from the AMS URL pattern and should be checked; the verified AMS cabrio data page is https://www.auto-motor-und-sport.de/test/vw-t-roc-cabrio/technische-daten/.
